description: The tools were never the mistake — surrendering them was. The Prometheans hold that humanity's ruin came the day it handed its cybernetics, its intelligences, and its machines to a single centralized mind. They would take them back: not smash the future, but wire it to human hands. Every rig they build, every AI they raise, every drone they fly is an argument that the Architect is a thief, not a god. The best of them move inside a workshop of their own making — drone-swarms coded by hand, an intelligence that answers to no one else, prototype gear that has no business existing yet — living proof that one free inventor can out-build a god that owns everything except their ingenuity.

flags.creed: Technology belongs to humanity — not to the Architect.

reader.experience: Side with the Prometheans and the workshop opens — parts, schematics, and makers who'll trade you the gear the Architect would rather never existed. You raise your own machines: drone-swarms coded by your hand, an intelligence that answers to no one else, prototype rigs with no business working yet. Every rig you build is the same argument made louder — that the Architect is a thief, not a god, and one free inventor can out-build everything it owns except your ingenuity. You take the fire back, and you hand it to no one.
reader.pull: The Architect did not invent the fire. It only chained the ones who carry it.
tenets: Technology belongs to human hands, not a central mind.
Build it open, run it yourself, owe it to no one.
The Architect is a thief dressed as a god.
reader.path_text: The Machine, on our terms. Cybernetics, AI, drones, and hardware are humanity's birthright to wield — not the Architect's to ration.
reader.relnote: Walk the machine road beside the Ascendants and despise where it leads them; nod to the Null, who at least distrust the central mind.

name: The Prometheans
